title.zh: 卷一百零九 列傳第三十四 崔楊竇宗祝王
title.en: Volume 109 Biographies 34: Cui, Yang, Dou, Zong, Hu, Wang
title.raw: 卷一百零九 列傳第三十四 崔楊竇宗祝王 Volume 109 Biographies 34: Cui, Yang, Dou, Zong, Hu, Wang

sentences.zh: 崔義玄，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan came from Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋大業亂，往見李密，密不用。

translations.literal: During the chaos of the Sui Daye reign, he went to see Li Mi, but Li Mi did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui empire collapsed in the Daye era, he sought out Li Mi, who declined to take him on.

sentences.zh: 河內賊黃君漢為密守柏崖，義玄見群鼠度河，

translations.literal: The bandit of Henei, Huang Junhan, held Baiya for Li Mi; Yixuan saw a swarm of rats crossing the river,
translations.idiomatic: Huang Junhan, a rebel leader in Henei, was holding Baiya for Li Mi when Yixuan noticed a mass of rats swimming across the river,

sentences.zh: 槊刃有華文，曰：「此王敦亡兆也。」

translations.literal: and saw floral patterns on spear blades; he said, "This is an omen of Wang Dun's downfall."
translations.idiomatic: and saw ornate patterns on the blades of spears. He declared, "This foretells the fall of Wang Dun."

sentences.zh: 因說君漢以城歸，乃拜君漢懷州刺史、行軍總管，以義玄為司馬。

translations.literal: He therefore persuaded Junhan to surrender the city; Junhan was then appointed Commandant of Huaizhou and Commander-in-Chief on campaign, with Yixuan as his military secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged Junhan to submit the city, whereupon Junhan was made Commandant of Huaizhou and campaign commander-in-chief, with Yixuan as his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 王世充將高毘寇河內，義玄擊走之，多下屯堡。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's general Gao Pi raided Henei; Yixuan repelled him and captured many garrison forts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong's general Gao Pi attacked Henei, Yixuan drove him off and took numerous fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 君漢以所掠子女金帛分之，拒不受。

translations.literal: Junhan offered him a share of the women, children, gold, and silk he had looted, but he refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Junhan tried to give him a portion of the captives and plunder, but he would not take any of it.

sentences.zh: 以功封清丘縣公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was created Duke of Qingqiu.

sentences.zh: 太宗討世充，數用其謀。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Shichong, he repeatedly used Yixuan's plans.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizong's campaign against Wang Shichong, his counsel was sought again and again.

sentences.zh: 東都平，轉隰州都督府長史。

translations.literal: After the eastern capital was pacified, he was transferred to be Chief Clerk of the Xizhou Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Once the eastern capital fell, he was appointed chief clerk of the Xizhou military governorship.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷左司郎中，兼韓王府長史，與王友孟神慶誌趣不同，而俱以介直任。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he served successively as Director of the Left Bureau and concurrently as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Han; though his aspirations differed from those of the prince's companion Meng Shenqing, both were appointed for their upright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he rose through the Left Bureau and served concurrently as chief clerk to the Prince of Han. He and the prince's friend Meng Shenqing did not see eye to eye, yet both were valued for their blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，累遷婺州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era he was repeatedly promoted, eventually becoming Governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui period he advanced step by step until he became governor of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時睦州女子陳碩真舉兵反。

translations.literal: At that time the woman of Muzhou, Chen Shuozhen, raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: About then Chen Shuozhen, a woman from Muzhou, took up arms in revolt.

sentences.zh: 始，碩真自言仙去，與鄉鄰辭訣，或告其詐，已而捕得，詔釋不問。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shuozhen had claimed she would ascend as an immortal and bade farewell to her neighbors; someone reported the fraud, and she was soon captured, but an edict ordered her released without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: She had once announced that she was leaving the world as an immortal and said goodbye to her neighbors. When someone exposed the trick, she was caught, but the court let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 於是姻家章叔胤妄言碩真自天還，化為男子，能役使鬼物，轉相熒惑，用是能幻眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon her kinsman by marriage Zhang Shuyin falsely declared that Shuozhen had returned from heaven, transformed into a man, and could command ghosts and spirits; rumor spread and deceived the masses, so that she could beguile crowds.
translations.idiomatic: Her relative by marriage Zhang Shuyin then spread the lie that she had come back from heaven as a man who could command spirits. The story passed from mouth to mouth until she could work her illusions on a multitude.

sentences.zh: 自稱文佳皇帝，以叔胤為僕射，破睦州，攻歙，殘之，分遣其黨圍婺州。

translations.literal: She styled herself Emperor Wenjia, appointed Shuyin as Puye, seized Muzhou, attacked She, ravaged it, and sent her followers in separate bands to besiege Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: She proclaimed herself Emperor Wenjia, made Shuyin her chief minister, overran Muzhou, stormed She and laid it waste, then sent factions of her force to encircle Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 義玄發兵拒之，其徒爭言碩真有神靈，犯其兵輒滅宗，眾兇懼不肯用。

translations.literal: Yixuan raised troops to resist; his men argued that Shuozhen had divine power and that anyone who attacked her army would have his whole clan destroyed, so the soldiers, terrified, refused to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan mobilized troops to meet her, but his men insisted that she was supernatural and that any who struck her host would be wiped out to the last kin. The army, cowed by this, would not advance.

sentences.zh: 司功參軍崔玄籍曰：「仗順起兵，猶無成；

translations.literal: The Registrar of Merit Cui Xuanji said, "Even armies raised in the name of righteousness often fail;
translations.idiomatic: His registrar Cui Xuanji said, "Even a righteous rising often comes to nothing;

sentences.zh: 此乃妖人，勢不持久。」

translations.literal: this is merely a sorceress, and her power cannot last."
translations.idiomatic: this woman is a mere charlatan, and her power will not endure."

sentences.zh: 義玄乃署玄籍先鋒，而自統眾繼之。

translations.literal: Yixuan then appointed Xuanji as vanguard commander and himself led the main force after him.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan made Xuanji his vanguard and followed at the head of the main body.

sentences.zh: 至下淮戍，擒其諜數十人。

translations.literal: When they reached the garrison at Xiahuai, they captured several dozen of her spies.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xiahuai post they seized dozens of her spies.

sentences.zh: 有星墜賊營，義玄曰：「賊必亡。」

translations.literal: A star fell into the rebel camp; Yixuan said, "The bandits are sure to perish."
translations.idiomatic: A meteor dropped into the rebel encampment. Yixuan said, "The rebels are finished."

sentences.zh: 詰朝奮擊，左右有以盾鄣者，義玄曰：「刺史而有避邪，誰肯死？」

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he pressed the attack fiercely; when attendants tried to shield him with shields, Yixuan said, "If a governor shrinks from harm, who will die for him?"
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he led a fierce assault. When men beside him raised shields to protect him, he said, "If the governor hides behind a shield, who will lay down his life?"

sentences.zh: 敕去之。

translations.literal: He ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded that they be taken away.

sentences.zh: 由是眾為用，斬首數百級，降其眾萬余。

translations.literal: Thereupon the troops gave their full effort; they beheaded several hundred and accepted the surrender of more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the men fought with all their heart, taking hundreds of heads and receiving the surrender of more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊平，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was made chief censor.

sentences.zh: 義玄有章句學，先儒疑繆，或音故不通者，輒采諸家，條分節解，能是正之。

translations.literal: Yixuan was skilled in exegetical learning; where earlier Confucians had doubts or errors, or where phonology and ancient usage were obscure, he would gather the schools, analyze passage by passage, and could set the text right.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan was a master of classical commentary. Where earlier scholars had been uncertain or where sound and usage blocked understanding, he drew on every school, divided the text into sections, and set it straight.

sentences.zh: 高宗詔與博士討論《五經》義。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ordered him to discuss the meaning of the Five Classics with the Erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong summoned him to debate the Five Classics with the court scholars.

sentences.zh: 武氏為皇后，義玄贊帝決，又以後旨按長孫無忌等誅之。

translations.literal: When the Wu clan's daughter became empress, Yixuan supported the emperor's decision, and on the empress's orders investigated and brought about the execution of Changsun Wuji and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wu became empress, Yixuan backed the emperor's resolve and, acting on her command, investigated Changsun Wuji and others until they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 終蒲州刺史，年七十一。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Governor of Puzhou and died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He finished his days as governor of Puzhou and died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州都督，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Military Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as military governor of Youzhou, with the temple name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 後持政，贈揚州大都督，賜其家實封戶二百。

translations.literal: When the empress later held power, he was posthumously made Grand Military Governor of Yangzhou, and his family was granted two hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: After she took firm control of government, he was posthumously raised to grand military governor of Yangzhou, and his household received a substantive fief of two hundred families.

sentences.zh: 子神基襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shenji inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenji succeeded to the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 神基，長壽中，為司賓卿、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Shenji, during the Changshou era, served as Minister of Ceremonial for Guests and as Chancellor of the Tong Fengge Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou period Shenji served as minister of ceremonial for guests and as a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 為酷吏所構，流嶺南。

translations.literal: He was framed by ruthless officials and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruthless prosecutors fabricated a case against him and he was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 中宗初，稍用為大理卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongzong's reign he was gradually reappointed as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhongzong's reign he was gradually brought back and made minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 弟神慶，舉明經，武後時，累遷萊州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shenqing passed the Mingjing examination; during Empress Wu's reign he was repeatedly promoted until he became Governor of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shenqing, a Mingjing graduate, rose under Empress Wu until he became governor of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 入朝，待制億歲殿，奏事稱旨。

translations.literal: When he entered court he waited on duty in the Hall of Ten Thousand Years; his memorials pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On coming to court he served as an attendant in the Hall of Ten Thousand Years, and his reports always pleased her.

sentences.zh: 後以歷官有佳政，且其父於己有功，擢拜并州長史，謂曰：「并州，朕鄉里，宿兵多，前長史皆尚書為之，今授卿，宜知所以委重者。」

translations.literal: Later, because of his excellent administration in successive posts and because his father had rendered service to her, he was promoted to Chief Clerk of Bingzhou; she said to him, "Bingzhou is my native place, with many garrison troops; former chief clerks were all ministers of the Ministry of Works. Now I appoint you—you should know why this trust is weighty."
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of his good record in office and his father's service to her, he was made chief clerk of Bingzhou. She told him, "Bingzhou is my home district and holds many troops. Former chief clerks were all ministers of works. I am giving it to you now; you should understand how heavy this charge is."

sentences.zh: 乃親為按行圖，謀日而遣。

translations.literal: She personally drew up a map from an inspection tour, planned the day of departure, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: She herself drew a map from an inspection tour, set the day of his departure, and dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 神慶始至，有詔改錢幣法，州縣布下，俄而物價踴昂，百賈驚擾，神慶質其非於朝，果豪猾妄為之。

translations.literal: When Shenqing had just arrived, an edict changed the currency law; the prefectures and counties promulgated it, and soon prices soared and merchants were thrown into alarm; Shenqing questioned the policy at court, and it proved that unscrupulous men had acted recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Shenqing took up his post, an edict changed the coinage. Counties and prefectures rushed to implement it, prices shot up, and traders panicked. Shenqing challenged the policy at court and proved that sharp dealers had abused it.

sentences.zh: 後喜，下制褒美。

translations.literal: The empress was pleased and issued an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was delighted and issued a decree praising him.

sentences.zh: 初，州隔汾為東、西二城，神慶跨水聯堞，合而一之，省防禦兵歲數千。

translations.literal: Earlier the prefecture had been divided by the Fen River into eastern and western cities; Shenqing linked battlements across the water and united them into one, saving several thousand defense troops each year.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long been split into eastern and western cities by the Fen. Shenqing joined their walls across the river into a single city and saved several thousand garrison troops a year.

sentences.zh: 神基既下獄，馳赴都告變，得召見，後出具獄示之，神慶為申理，得減死，然用是貶歙州司馬。

translations.literal: After Shenji was imprisoned, Shenqing rushed to the capital to report an emergency and gained an audience; the empress produced the prison records for him to see; Shenqing pleaded on his brother's behalf and secured a commutation of the death sentence, but for this he was demoted to military secretary of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenji was thrown into prison, Shenqing raced to the capital to report trouble and won an audience. The empress showed him the case file. He argued for his brother and won a reprieve from death, but was himself demoted to military secretary in Shezhou for his pains.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累轉禮部侍郎，數上疏陳時政。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he was repeatedly transferred until he became Vice Minister of Rites, and often submitted memorials on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an period he rose to vice minister of rites and sent up many memorials on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 轉太子右庶子，封魏縣子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and enfeoffed as Viscount of Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right vice director of the crown prince's household and created Viscount of Weixian.

sentences.zh: 是時，突厥使者入見，皇太子應朝，有司移文東宮召太子。

translations.literal: At that time envoys from the Turks came to audience; the crown prince was to attend court, and the relevant offices sent a document to the Eastern Palace summoning the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic envoys were then received at court, and the crown prince was expected to attend. The responsible offices sent a formal summons to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 神慶諫曰：「五品以上佩龜者，蓋防征召之詐，內出龜以合之，況太子乎？

translations.literal: Shenqing remonstrated, saying, "Those of the fifth rank and above who wear tortoise insignia do so to guard against fraudulent summons; an insignia issued from within must match—how much more so for the crown prince?
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing objected: "Officials of the fifth rank and above wear tortoise insignia precisely to prevent forged summonses—the court issues a matching token. Should not the same hold for the crown prince?

sentences.zh: 古者召太子用玉契，此誠重慎防萌之意，不可不察。

translations.literal: In antiquity the crown prince was summoned with a jade tally; this truly expresses the intent to be weightily cautious and to guard against what is nascent—it must not be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times the crown prince was summoned with a jade tally. That was careful forethought against the first stirrings of trouble, and we must not ignore it.

sentences.zh: 凡慮事於未萌之前，故長無悔吝之咎。

translations.literal: In general, by considering matters before they sprout, one can long avoid the fault of regret.
translations.idiomatic: When troubles are headed off before they appear, remorse seldom follows.

sentences.zh: 今太子與陛下異宮，非朝朔望而別喚者，請降墨敕玉契。」

translations.literal: Now the crown prince dwells in a separate palace from Your Majesty; when he is summoned outside the first and fifteenth of the month, I beg that an imperial decree in vermilion ink with a jade tally be issued."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince now lives apart from Your Majesty. Whenever he is called outside the regular audience days, I ask that a vermilion edict with a jade tally be sent."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 尋詔與詹事祝欽明更日侍讀東宮。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered, together with the Household Mentor Zhu Qinming, to serve the Eastern Palace as readers on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and the crown prince's mentor Zhu Qinming were ordered to take turns lecturing at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 歷司刑卿，劾張昌宗獄，頗闊略不盡。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Punishments and prosecuted the case of Zhang Changzong, but his investigation was rather broad and incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of punishments he handled the case against Zhang Changzong, but his inquiry was loose and left much undone.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，昌宗伏誅，坐流欽州，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Changzong was executed; Shenqing was implicated and exiled to Qinzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Changzong was put to death. Shenqing was implicated, exiled to Qinzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 五王得罪，緣昌宗被流者皆詔原雪，贈神慶幽州都督。

translations.literal: When the Five Princes were punished, all who had been exiled on account of Changzong were pardoned by edict; Shenqing was posthumously made Military Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Five Princes fell, everyone banished because of Changzong was cleared by edict, and Shenqing was posthumously named military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 神慶子琳，明政事，開元中，與高仲舒同為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shenqing's son Lin understood government affairs; during Kaiyuan he served together with Gao Zhongshu as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing's son Lin was skilled in administration. In the Kaiyuan era he and Gao Zhongshu both served as secretariat drafters.

sentences.zh: 侍中宋璟親禮之，每所訪逮，嘗曰：「古事問仲舒，今事問琳，尚何疑？」

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Jing treated him with personal respect; whenever he sought advice he would say, "For antiquity ask Zhongshu; for the present ask Lin—what doubt remains?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Song Jing honored him personally. Whenever he sought counsel he would say, "Ask Zhongshu about the past and Lin about the present—what is left to doubt?"

sentences.zh: 累遷太子少保。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted until he became Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年卒，秘書監潘肅聞之，泫然曰：「古遺愛也！」

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Tianbao; when the Director of the Secretariat Pan Su heard of it, he wept and said, "This is a man of ancient benevolence!"
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianbao 2. Pan Su, director of the secretariat, wept when he heard the news and said, "A man of the old school of public love!"

sentences.zh: 琳長子儼，諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Lin's eldest son Yan became Remonstrance Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan became a remonstrance councillor.

sentences.zh: 其群從數十人，自興寧裏謁大明宮，冠蓋騶哄相望。

translations.literal: Several dozen of his clan and followers, from Xingning Lane, went to pay homage at Daming Palace; officials in caps and carriages with escorts stretched in an unbroken line.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of his kinsmen and followers from Xingning Lane would call at Daming Palace, their coaches and outriders filling the road without a break.

sentences.zh: 每歲時宴於家，以一榻置笏，猶重積其上。

translations.literal: Each year at seasonal feasts in his home he would set out one couch for official tablets, yet still pile them high upon it.
translations.idiomatic: At his yearly family banquets he set out a single couch for court tablets, yet still heaped them until they overflowed.

sentences.zh: 琳與弟太子詹事珪、光祿卿瑤俱列棨戟，世號「三戟崔家」。

translations.literal: Lin, together with his younger brothers the Crown Prince's Household Director Gui and the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Yao, all displayed ceremonial halberds at their gates; the age called them "the Three-Halberd Cui family."
translations.idiomatic: Lin and his brothers Gui, director of the crown prince's household, and Yao, minister of imperial sacrifices, all bore ceremonial halberds at their gates, and the world spoke of the "Three-Halberd Cui."

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間，中外宗屬無緦麻喪。

translations.literal: Between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, among their kin inside and outside the clan there was no mourning even of the lightest degree.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns, not one of their kin near or far went into even the briefest mourning.

sentences.zh: 初，玄宗每命相，皆先書其名，一日書琳等名，覆以金甌，會太子入，帝謂曰：「此宰相名，若自意之，誰乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, whenever Xuanzong appointed a chancellor he would first write the name; one day he wrote the names of Lin and others and covered them with a golden bowl; when the crown prince entered, the emperor said, "These are the names of future chancellors—if you guess by your own judgment, who are they?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong used to write down the names of men he meant to make chancellor. One day he wrote Lin's name among others and covered the list with a golden bowl. When the crown prince came in, the emperor said, "Here are the next chancellors. Who do you think they are?

sentences.zh: 即中，且賜酒。」

translations.literal: If you hit the mark, I shall also grant you wine."
translations.idiomatic: Guess right and I will give you wine."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「非崔琳、盧從願乎？」

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "Are they not Cui Lin and Lu Congyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Surely Cui Lin and Lu Congyuan?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is."

sentences.zh: 賜太子酒。

translations.literal: He granted the crown prince wine.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the crown prince wine.

sentences.zh: 時兩人有宰相望，帝欲相之數矣，以族大，恐附離者眾，卒不用。

translations.literal: At that time both men had the reputation of future chancellors; the emperor had wished to appoint them several times, but because their clan was large he feared many would attach themselves to them, and in the end did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Both were thought destined for the highest office, and the emperor had nearly appointed them more than once, but their clan was so large that he feared a crowd of hangers-on and never did.

sentences.zh: 楊再思，鄭州原武人，第明經，為人佞而智。

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi was a native of Yuanwu in Zhengzhou; he passed the Mingjing examination and was a man both sycophantic and clever.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi came from Yuanwu in Zhengzhou, held the Mingjing degree, and was at once servile and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 初，調玄武尉，使至京師，舍逆旅，有盜竊其衣囊，再思遇之，盜窘謝。

translations.literal: Early on he was assigned as an assistant in Xuanwu and sent on duty to the capital; he lodged at an inn, and a thief stole his clothing and bag; Zaisi encountered him, and the thief, embarrassed, apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career he served as an assistant in Xuanwu and was sent to the capital. At an inn a thief stole his baggage. Zaisi caught him, and the man stammered an apology.

sentences.zh: 再思曰：「而苦貧，故至此。

translations.literal: Zaisi said, "You suffer bitter poverty, hence you have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi said, "You are desperately poor, and that is why you did this.

sentences.zh: 囊中檄無所事，幸留，它物可持去。」

translations.literal: The documents in the bag are of no use to you—please leave them; you may take the other things."
translations.idiomatic: The papers in the bag are useless to you—keep them if you will, but take whatever else you need."

sentences.zh: 初不為人言，但假貸以還。

translations.literal: At first he told no one, but borrowed money to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: He told no one at first, but borrowed money to replace what had been taken.

sentences.zh: 累遷天官員外郎，歷左肅政御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Wai Lang in the Ministry of Personnel and served as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left Office of Imperial Censors.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to an outer-office post in the ministry of personnel and served as left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 延載初，擢鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，加兼左肅政御史大夫，封鄭縣侯，遷內史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai he was promoted to Vice Minister of Luantai and Chancellor of Tong Fengge Luantai, additionally made concurrently Director of the Left Office of Imperial Censors, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhengxian, and transferred to Neishi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanzai era he became vice minister of Luantai and chancellor, was also named chief of the left censorate, created Marquis of Zhengxian, and made head of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居宰相十余年，阿匼取容，無所薦達。

translations.literal: He held the chancellorship for more than ten years, flattering and currying favor, and recommended no one for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He remained chancellor for more than ten years, fawning on everyone in power and advancing no one of merit.

sentences.zh: 人主所不喜，毀之；

translations.literal: Whomever the ruler disliked, he denounced;
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign disliked someone, he tore him down;

sentences.zh: 所善，譽之。

translations.literal: whomever he favored, he praised.
translations.idiomatic: if the sovereign favored someone, he praised him to the skies.

sentences.zh: 畏慎足恭，未嘗忤物。

translations.literal: He was fearful, cautious, and thoroughly deferential, and never offended anyone.
translations.idiomatic: He was timid, careful, and elaborately polite, and never crossed anyone.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「公位尊，何自屈折？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "Your position is exalted—why do you humble yourself so?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "You stand so high—why abase yourself like this?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「世路孔艱，直者先禍。

translations.literal: He answered, "The path of the world is exceedingly hard; the upright meet disaster first.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The world is a narrow road, and the straight-spoken are ruined first.

sentences.zh: 不爾，豈全吾軀？」

translations.literal: Otherwise, how could I preserve my body?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how would I keep my skin whole?"

sentences.zh: 於時水沴，閉坊門以禳。

translations.literal: At that time there was a flood calamity, and neighborhood gates were closed for exorcistic rites.
translations.idiomatic: There was flooding then, and ward gates were shut for ritual appeasement.

sentences.zh: 再思入朝，有車陷於濘，叱牛不前，恚曰：「癡宰相不能和陰陽，而閉坊門，遣我艱於行！」

translations.literal: When Zaisi went to court, a carriage sank in the mud; he scolded the oxen for not moving forward and angrily said, "This foolish chancellor cannot harmonize yin and yang, yet closes ward gates and makes my journey hard!"
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi was going to court when his cart sank in the mire. He whipped the oxen and cried, "That idiot chancellor cannot balance heaven and earth, yet he shuts the ward gates and leaves me stuck in the mud!"

sentences.zh: 再思遣吏謂曰：「汝牛自弱，不得獨責宰相。」

translations.literal: Zaisi sent an official to say to him, "Your oxen are simply weak—you cannot blame the chancellor alone."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi sent a clerk to tell him, "Your oxen are feeble; you cannot lay all of this on the chancellor."

sentences.zh: 張昌宗坐事，司刑少卿桓彥範劾免其官，昌宗訴諸朝，武後意申釋之，問宰相：「昌宗於國有功乎？」

translations.literal: Zhang Changzong was implicated in a case; the Vice Minister of Punishments Huan Yanfan impeached him and had him removed from office; Changzong appealed at court; Empress Wu intended to release him and asked the chancellors, "Has Changzong rendered service to the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changzong fell under investigation. Vice minister of punishments Huan Yanfan impeached him and stripped him of office. Changzong appealed to court, and Empress Wu meant to let him off. She asked the chancellors, "Has Changzong served the state?"

sentences.zh: 再思曰：「昌宗為陛下治丹，餌而愈，此為有功。」

translations.literal: Zaisi said, "Changzong prepared elixirs for Your Majesty; after you took them you recovered—this is meritorious service."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi said, "He compounded elixirs for Your Majesty. You took them and were cured. That is service to the state."

sentences.zh: 後悅，昌宗還官。

translations.literal: The empress was pleased, and Changzong regained his post.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was pleased, and Changzong was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 自是天下貴彥範，賤再思。

translations.literal: From then on the empire esteemed Yanfan and despised Zaisi.
translations.idiomatic: After that the world honored Yanfan and held Zaisi in contempt.

sentences.zh: 左補闕戴令言賦「兩腳狐」以譏之，再思怒，謫令言為長社令，士愈蚩噪。

translations.literal: The Left Remonstrance Councillor Dai Lingyan composed a piece titled "Two-legged Fox" to satirize him; Zaisi was angry and exiled Lingyan as magistrate of Changshe, which only made scholars mock him more loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Left remonstrance councillor Dai Lingyan wrote a satire called "The Two-legged Fox." Zaisi in a rage banished him to be magistrate of Changshe, and the literati only laughed the louder.

sentences.zh: 易之兄司禮少卿同休，請公卿宴其寺，酒酣，戲曰：「公面似高麗。」

translations.literal: Yizhi's elder brother, the Vice Minister of Rites Tongxiu, invited the high officials to a feast at his temple; when the wine was deep, he jested, "Your face resembles Goguryeo."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi's elder brother Tongxiu, vice minister of rites, entertained the chief ministers at his temple. Deep in wine, he joked, "Your face looks rather Korean."

sentences.zh: 再思欣然，翦谷綴巾上，反披紫袍，為高麗舞，舉動合節，滿坐鄙笑。

translations.literal: Zaisi was delighted; he cut grain stalks and fastened them to his headcloth, turned his purple robe inside out, and performed a Goguryeo dance with movements in perfect rhythm, to the scornful laughter of the whole assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi beamed, trimmed stalks to pin on his cap, wore his purple robe inside out, and danced a Korean step in perfect time while the whole table sneered.

sentences.zh: 昌宗以姿貌得幸，再思每曰：「人言六郎似蓮華，非也；

translations.literal: Changzong gained favor through his looks; Zaisi would often say, "People say the Sixth Lord resembles the lotus—that is not so;
translations.idiomatic: Changzong won favor by his beauty. Zaisi would say, "People claim the Sixth Lord looks like a lotus blossom. They have it backward;

sentences.zh: 正謂蓮華似六郎耳。」

translations.literal: it should be said that the lotus resembles the Sixth Lord."
translations.idiomatic: the lotus resembles the Sixth Lord."

sentences.zh: 其巧諛無恥類如此。

translations.literal: His artful flattery and shamelessness were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His sycophancy was as shameless as this.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校右庶子。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named acting right vice director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，拜戶部尚書、同中書門下三品、京師留守，封弘農郡公，加兼揚州長史，檢校中書令。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was enthroned, [Zaisi] was appointed Minister of Revenue, Vice Chairman of the Chancellery under the Three Departments, and Resident Commissioner of the Capital; enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong; additionally made concurrent Chief Administrator of Yangzhou and Acting Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong took the throne, Zaisi was made minister of revenue, vice chairman of the chancellery under the Three Departments, and resident commissioner of the capital; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong, given the concurrent post of chief administrator of Yangzhou, and named acting director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 改侍中，鄭國公，賜實封戶三百，為順天皇后奉冊使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Palace Attendant, Duke of Zheng, granted three hundred households of substantive fief, and made commissioner to present the memorial register to Empress Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made palace attendant and Duke of Zheng, granted three hundred taxpaying households, and appointed commissioner to present the empress's memorial register.

sentences.zh: 武三思誣陷王同晈，再思與李嶠、韋巨源按獄，希意抵同晈死，眾以為冤。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi falsely incriminated Wang Tongjiao; Zaisi, together with Li Qiao and Wei Juyuan, investigated the case, reading the emperor's wish to have Tongjiao condemned to death; the multitude regarded it as a miscarriage of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sansi framed Wang Tongjiao, Zaisi joined Li Qiao and Wei Juyuan in trying the case, bending the verdict to satisfy the court and send Tongjiao to his death; many believed an innocent man had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 復拜中書令，監修國史。

translations.literal: Again appointed Director of the Chancellery and put in charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made director of the chancellery and superintendent of the national history.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，仍同三品。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, still with rank as one of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the department of state affairs while retaining his standing among the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈特進、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Special Advancement and Great Area Commander of Bingzhou; buried alongside Qianling; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as special advancement and great area commander of Bingzhou, buried near Qianling, and given the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 弟季昭，中茂才第，為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jizhao passed the provincial Outstanding Talent examination and served as Palace Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jizhao passed the provincial "Outstanding Talent" examination and became a palace investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 武後誅駙馬都尉薛紹，紹兄顗為齊州刺史，命季昭按之，不得反狀，後怒，放於沙州。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu executed Commandant-Consort Xue Shao, Shao's elder brother Yan was Prefect of Qizhou; she ordered Jizhao to investigate him but he found no evidence of treason; the empress was angered and banished him to Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu executed the commandant-consort Xue Shao, she ordered Jizhao to investigate Shao's elder brother Yan, prefect of Qizhou; finding no proof of rebellion, he was sent in the empress's wrath into exile at Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 赦還，為懷州司馬。

translations.literal: After an amnesty he was recalled and made Military Secretary of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled under a general pardon, he served as military secretary of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 竇懷貞，字從一，左相德玄子。

translations.literal: Dou Huaizhen, courtesy name Congyi, was the son of Left Chancellor Dou Dexuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Huaizhen, styled Congyi, was the son of the left chancellor Dou Dexuan.

sentences.zh: 少詭激，衣服羸儉，不為輿馬豪侈事。

translations.literal: In youth he was eccentric and excitable; his clothing was worn and plain; he did not indulge in the luxury of carriages and horses.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was odd and impulsive, dressed in threadbare clothes, and shunned the extravagance of fine carriages and horses.

sentences.zh: 仕累清河令，有治狀。

translations.literal: In office he rose through successive posts to Magistrate of Qinghe, with a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In service he worked his way up to magistrate of Qinghe, where he earned a reputation for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 後遷越州都督、揚州長史。

translations.literal: Later promoted to Area Commander of Yuezhou and Chief Administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to area commander of Yuezhou and chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，進左御史大夫兼檢校雍州長史。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era, advanced to Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Acting Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong period he rose to left censor-in-chief and acting chief administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 會歲除，中宗夜宴近臣，謂曰：「聞卿喪妻，今欲繼室可乎？」

translations.literal: It happened to be year-end; Zhongzong gave a night banquet for close ministers and said: "I hear you have lost your wife—would you now wish to remarry?"
translations.idiomatic: At the year's end Zhongzong held a night banquet for his inner circle and said, "I hear your wife has died. Would you like to take another?"

sentences.zh: 懷貞唯唯。

translations.literal: Huaizhen assented repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen murmured his assent.

sentences.zh: 俄而禁中寶扇鄣衛，有衣翟衣出者，已乃韋後乳媼王，所謂莒國夫人者，故蠻婢也。

translations.literal: Soon within the palace precincts, pearl-lattice screens and guards appeared, and someone in a pheasant-embroidered robe came forth—it was the wet nurse Wang of Empress Wei, known as Lady of Ju, formerly a barbarian slave girl.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the inner palace was screened with jeweled fans and attendants, and a woman in pheasant-embroidered robes emerged: Wang, wet nurse to Empress Wei and titled Lady of Ju, once a barbarian bondwoman.

sentences.zh: 懷貞納之不辭。

translations.literal: Huaizhen accepted her in marriage without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen took her as his wife without protest.

sentences.zh: 又避後先諱，而以字稱。

translations.literal: He also avoided the taboo on the empress's given name and addressed himself by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: He also avoided the empress's personal name and referred to himself by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 世謂媼婿為阿赩，懷貞每謁見奏請，輒自署「皇后阿赩」，而人或謂為「國赩」，軒然不訴，以自媚於後。

translations.literal: The world called a wet nurse's son-in-law "Axi"; whenever Huaizhen presented petitions at audience he signed himself "Axi of the Empress"; some called him "State Axi"; he showed no displeasure, using this to curry favor with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: People called a wet nurse's son-in-law "Axi." At every audience Huaizhen signed his memorials "the Empress's Axi"; wits shortened this to "State Axi." He preened rather than protested, flattering the empress by the title.

sentences.zh: 時政令多門，赤尉由墨制授御史者眾，或戲曰：「尉入臺多，而縣辦否？」

translations.literal: At the time policy came from many quarters; many county magistrates of the capital region were appointed censors by black-edict edicts; someone jested: "Many magistrates enter the Censorate—can the counties still be governed?"
translations.idiomatic: Government then issued from many hands, and numerous capital-district magistrates were made censors by informal edict. Someone joked, "So many magistrates have gone to the Censorate—can their counties still be run?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「辦於異日。」

translations.literal: [Huaizhen] replied: "They will be governed on another day."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "They will be run well enough—just not today."

sentences.zh: 問其故，答曰：「佳吏在，僥幸去，故辦。」

translations.literal: Asked the reason, he answered: "The good officials remain; the opportunists have gone—therefore they can be governed."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he said, "The capable men stay behind while the lucky climbers leave. That is why the counties will be all right."

sentences.zh: 聞者皆笑。

translations.literal: All who heard laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard him laughed.

sentences.zh: 又附宗楚客、安樂公主等以取貴位，為素議所斥，名稱盡矣。

translations.literal: He also attached himself to Zong Chuke, Princess Anle, and others to gain high position; upright critics condemned him, and his reputation was utterly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: He also clung to Zong Chuke, Princess Anle, and their like to climb higher, until upright opinion reviled him and his name was utterly spent.

sentences.zh: 韋後敗，斬妻獻其首，貶濠州司馬，再徙益州長史，乃復故名。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei fell, he beheaded his wife and presented her head; demoted to Military Secretary of Haozhou; later transferred to Chief Administrator of Yizhou; only then did he resume his original name.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wei's downfall he cut off his wife's head and offered it up; he was demoted to military secretary of Haozhou, then moved to chief administrator of Yizhou, and only then returned to his own name.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，以殿中監召，閱月遷左御史大夫、同中書門下平章事，封中山縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun, recalled as Director of the Palace Administration; within a month promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and Associate Director of the Chancellery and Palace Secretariat; enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun era he was recalled as director of the palace administration; within a month he became left censor-in-chief and associate director of the chancellery and palace secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍中。

translations.literal: Again promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 方太平公主干政，懷貞傾己附離，日視事退，輒詣主第，刺取所欲。

translations.literal: Just as Princess Taiping intervened in government, Huaizhen devoted himself wholly to attaching to her; each day after finishing official business he would go to the princess's residence to probe and obtain what she desired.
translations.idiomatic: While Princess Taiping held the reins of power, Huaizhen threw himself into her service; each day after court he went straight to her mansion to sound out and supply her wishes.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為金仙、玉真二公主營觀，費鉅萬，諫者交疏不止，唯懷貞勸成之，躬護役作。

translations.literal: Ruizong built monasteries for Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen at enormous expense; remonstrators submitted memorial after memorial without cease; only Huaizhen urged completion, personally overseeing the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong was building monasteries for Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen at colossal cost; memorials of remonstrance piled up, but Huaizhen alone urged the work on and personally supervised the construction.

sentences.zh: 族弟維鍌諫曰：「公位上袞，當思獻可替否輔天子，而計校瓦木，雜廁工匠間，使海內何所瞻仰乎？」

translations.literal: His clansman younger cousin Weilian remonstrated: "Sir, you hold one of the highest ministerial robes; you should think of offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not to assist the Son of Heaven—yet you haggle over tiles and timber and mingle among the craftsmen—what is there in the empire for people to look up to?"
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Weilian admonished him: "You wear one of the highest ministerial robes. You ought to speak what is fit and reject what is not on the Son of Heaven's behalf—not count tiles and beams and stand among laborers. What will the realm have to respect?"

sentences.zh: 不答，督繕益急。

translations.literal: He gave no answer and pressed the construction ever more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: He made no reply and drove the work harder still.

sentences.zh: 時語曰：「前作後國赩，後為主邑丞。」

translations.literal: A saying of the time ran: "First he was the empress's State Axi; afterward he became the princess's district assistant."
translations.idiomatic: People said at the time, "First he was the empress's State Axi; later he became the princess's district aide."

sentences.zh: 言事公主如邑官屬也。

translations.literal: Meaning that he served the princess like a subordinate local official.
translations.idiomatic: The point was that he waited on the princess like a county subordinate.

sentences.zh: 在位半歲，無所事，帝引見承天門，切責之。

translations.literal: After half a year in office with nothing accomplished, the emperor summoned him before Chengtian Gate and sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year passed with nothing to show for his tenure; the emperor had him brought before Chengtian Gate and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 俄與李日知、郭元振、張說皆罷。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed together with Li Rizhi, Guo Yuanzhen, and Zhang Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was removed from office along with Li Rizhi, Guo Yuanzhen, and Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 為左御史大夫。

translations.literal: [He was appointed] Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He retained the post of left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 於時，歲犯左執法，術家又言懷貞且有禍，大懼，表請為安國寺奴，不許。

translations.literal: At that time the planet Jupiter transgressed the Left Law-enforcer asterism, and diviners also said Huaizhen would soon meet disaster; greatly afraid, he memorialized requesting to become a slave of Anguo Temple—it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: About then Jupiter crossed the Left Law-enforcer star, and diviners warned that Huaizhen was headed for ruin; in terror he asked to be made a bondsman of Anguo Temple, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復同中書門下三品，兼太子詹事，監修國史。

translations.literal: After a year he again became Vice Chairman of the Chancellery under the Three Departments, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and superintendent of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was again vice chairman of the chancellery under the Three Departments, concurrently grand mentor of the crown prince and superintendent of the national history.

sentences.zh: 又以尚書右僕射兼御史大夫，軍國重事宜共平章。

translations.literal: Also made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Censor-in-Chief; weighty matters of army and state were to be jointly deliberated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made right vice director of the department of state affairs and censor-in-chief, with military and state affairs of first importance to be decided in consultation with him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗受內禪，進左僕射，封魏國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong received the inner abdication, [Huaizhen] was promoted to Left Vice Director and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong accepted the inner transfer of the throne, Huaizhen was promoted to left vice director and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 與太平公主謀逆，既敗，投水死，追戮其屍，改姓毒氏。

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion with Princess Taiping; once defeated he threw himself into water and died; his corpse was exhumed and mutilated in punishment; his surname was changed to Du, "Poison."
translations.idiomatic: He conspired with Princess Taiping in treason; when the plot failed he drowned himself, but his body was dug up and desecrated, and his clan name was changed to Du, "Poison."

sentences.zh: 然生平所得俸祿，悉散親族無留蓄，敗時，家惟粗米數石而已。

translations.literal: Yet the salary he received throughout his life he distributed entirely among his kin without keeping any in reserve; when he fell, his household had only a few piculs of coarse rice.
translations.idiomatic: All the same, every stipend he ever drew he gave away to kinsmen and kept nothing; when he fell, his house held only a few measures of coarse rice.

sentences.zh: 性諂詐，善諧結權貴，宦者用事，尤所畏奉，或見無須者，誤為之禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was sycophantic and deceitful, skilled at bonding with the powerful; eunuchs held power and he particularly feared and honored them—or upon seeing a beardless man he would mistakenly salute him as a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature a flatterer and a schemer, adept at courting the mighty; eunuchs especially he feared and fawned upon, and he would sometimes bow to a beardless man by mistake.

sentences.zh: 監察御史魏傳弓嫉中人輔信義，欲劾奏其奸，懷貞曰：「是安樂所信任者，奈何繩之？」

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wei Chuanggong hated the eunuch Fu Xinyi and wished to impeach his corruption; Huaizhen said: "This is one whom Princess Anle trusts—how can you bind him with the law?"
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Wei Chuanggong despised the eunuch Fu Xinyi and meant to impeach him for corruption. Huaizhen said, "That man is trusted by Princess Anle. How can you hold him to account?"

sentences.zh: 傳弓曰：「王綱壞矣，正坐此屬。

translations.literal: Chuanggong said: "The royal net is already broken—and it is precisely because of men like these.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanggong replied, "The dynasty's laws are in ruins, and it is precisely because of creatures like him.

sentences.zh: 今日殺之，明日誅，無所悔！」

translations.literal: Kill him today, and if I am executed tomorrow, I shall have no regrets!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill him today, and if I am put to death tomorrow, I will not repent!"

sentences.zh: 懷貞猶固止之。

translations.literal: Huaizhen still stubbornly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen still blocked him firmly.

sentences.zh: 傳弓者，鉅鹿人，忠謇士也，終司農丞。

translations.literal: As for Chuanggong, he was a man of Julu, a loyal and outspoken gentleman, and ended as Vice Director of the Directorate of Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanggong was from Julu, a man of loyalty and blunt integrity, and ended his career as vice director of the directorate of grain.

sentences.zh: 懷貞從子兢，字思慎，舉明經，為英王府參軍、尚乘直長。

translations.literal: Huaizhen's nephew Jing, courtesy name Shenshen, passed the Classics examination and served as Adjutant in the Prince of Ying's household and Chief of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen's nephew Jing, styled Shenshen, passed the classics examination and served in the household of the Prince of Ying and as chief of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 調郪令，修郵舍道路，設冠婚喪紀法，百姓德之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Magistrate of Zi, he repaired postal stations and roads, established regulations for capping, marriage, and mourning, and the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as magistrate of Zi, he rebuilt post stations and roads, set rules for coming-of-age, wedding, and funeral rites, and the people blessed him for it.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客，字叔敖，其先南陽人。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke, courtesy name Shu'ao—the family's ancestral home was Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke, styled Shu'ao, traced his ancestry to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖丕，後梁南弘農太守，梁亡入隋，居河東之汾陰，故為蒲州人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Pi was Southern Hongnong Prefect under Later Liang; when Liang fell he entered Sui and settled at Fenyin in Hedong, hence [the family] were men of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Pi had been southern Hongnong prefect under Later Liang; after Liang's fall he entered Sui service and settled at Fenyin in Hedong, so the clan came to be counted as men of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 父岌，仕魏王泰府，與謝偃等撰《括地志》。

translations.literal: His father Ba served in the household of Prince of Wei Tai and with Xie Yan and others compiled the Comprehensive Geography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ba served in the household of Prince Tai of Wei and, with Xie Yan and others, compiled the Comprehensive Geography.

sentences.zh: 楚客，武後從姊子，長六尺八寸，明皙美須髯。

translations.literal: Chuke was a nephew of Empress Wu's elder female cousin by marriage; he stood six feet eight inches, with a clear complexion and handsome beard and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was a nephew on the Wu side through the empress's elder cousin by marriage; he stood six feet eight inches tall, with a bright complexion and a fine beard.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，累遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed the Jinshi examination and rose through successive promotions to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the jinshi degree he rose step by step to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 兄秦客，垂拱中，勸武後革命，進為內史，而弟晉卿典羽林兵。

translations.literal: His elder brother Qinke, during the Chuigong era, urged Empress Wu to change the dynasty; he advanced to Grand Secretary, while younger brother Jinqing controlled the Feathered Forest army.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qinke, in the Chuigong years, urged Empress Wu to seize the throne; he rose to grand secretary while the younger brother Jinqing commanded the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 後兄弟並坐奸贓流嶺外。

translations.literal: Later the brothers were all convicted of corruption and banished beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Later the brothers were all convicted of graft and sent into exile beyond the Ling range.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，秦客死，而楚客等還。

translations.literal: After more than a year Qinke died, and Chuke and the others were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year on, Qinke died, and Chuke and the rest were brought back.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校夏官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Soon made Acting Vice Minister of the Ministry of War and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting vice minister of war and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.

sentences.zh: 與武懿宗不協，會賜將作材營第，僭侈過度，為懿宗所劾，自文昌左丞貶播州司馬，晉卿流峰州。

translations.literal: He fell out with Wu Yizong; when he was granted imperial lumber from the Construction Office to build a residence with excessive extravagance, Yizong impeached him; demoted from Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat to Military Secretary of Bozhou; Jinqing exiled to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Wu Yizong; when imperial building timber was granted him for a mansion far beyond proper scale, Yizong impeached him. Chuke was demoted from left assistant director of the secretariat to military secretary of Bozhou, and Jinqing was exiled to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍為豫州長史，遷少府少監、岐陜二州刺史。

translations.literal: After a time made Chief Administrator of Yuzhou; promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshop and Prefect of Qi and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: After a while he became chief administrator of Yuzhou, then vice director of the palace workshops and prefect of Qi and Shan.

sentences.zh: 久之，復以夏官侍郎同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: After a long while again made Vice Minister of War and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he again became vice minister of war and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.

sentences.zh: 坐聘邵王妓，貶原州都督。

translations.literal: Convicted of taking a courtesan from Prince Shao's household; demoted to Area Commander of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for taking a courtesan from Prince Shao's household and demoted to area commander of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為太僕卿、郢國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, made Minister of the Stud and Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era he became minister of the stud and Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 武三思引為兵部尚書，以晉卿為將作大匠。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi brought him in as Minister of War and made Jinqing Grand Master of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi installed him as minister of war and made Jinqing grand master of construction.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子敗，逃於鄠，被殺，殊其首祭三思等柩，楚客請之也。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Jiemin was defeated, [the prince] fled to E and was killed; his severed head was offered before the coffins of Sansi and others—at Chuke's request.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Jiemin's defeat the prince fled to E and was slain; at Chuke's request his severed head was displayed before the coffins of Sansi and the rest.

sentences.zh: 俄同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Soon made Vice Chairman of the Chancellery under the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice chairman of the chancellery under the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 韋後、安樂公主親賴之，與紀處訥為黨，世號「宗紀」。

translations.literal: Empress Wei and Princess Anle relied on him intimately; he formed a faction with Ji Chuna, and the age called them "Zong-Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei and Princess Anle leaned on him heavily; he and Ji Chuna formed a clique known in the age as "Zong-Ji."

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，詔突厥娑葛為金河郡王，而其部闕啜忠節賂楚客等罷之，娑葛怨，將兵患邊。

translations.literal: In Jinglong year 2, an edict enfeoffed the Turk Soge as Prince of Jinhe commandery; but his subordinate Quechuo Zhongjie bribed Chuke and others to have him removed; Soge resented this and led troops to trouble the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong an edict made the Turk Soge prince of Jinhe commandery, but his subordinate Quechuo Zhongjie bribed Chuke and his allies to have the appointment revoked; Soge, enraged, marched and harassed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 監察御史崔琬廷奏：「楚客、處訥專威福，有無君心，納境外交，為國取怨；

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Cui Wan memorialized at court: "Chuke and Chuna monopolize authority and favor, harbor disloyal intent toward the sovereign, accept bribes from beyond the border, and bring resentment upon the state;
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Cui Wan memorialized at court: "Chuke and Chuna hoard power and favor, show a heart that sets itself above the sovereign, take bribes from beyond the border, and bring the state's enemies upon us;

sentences.zh: 晉卿專徇贓私，驕恣跋扈。

translations.literal: Jinqing devotes himself to corrupt private gain and is arrogant, willful, and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing pursues illicit profit alone, arrogant and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 並請收付獄，三司推鞫。」

translations.literal: All three should be arrested and imprisoned for investigation by the Three Departments."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all three be seized and handed to the Three Departments for trial."

sentences.zh: 故事，大臣為御史對仗彈劾，必趨出，立朝堂待罪。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a minister was impeached by a censor in formal audience, he had to hurry out and stand in the court hall awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a censor impeached a minister in formal audience, the minister had to leave the hall at once and stand outside awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 楚客乃厲色大言：「性忠鯁，為琬誣詆。」

translations.literal: Chuke then spoke loudly in a harsh tone: "By nature I am loyal and upright—I am slandered by Wan."
translations.idiomatic: Chuke answered in a harsh, ringing voice: "I am by nature loyal and blunt—Wan has defamed me."

sentences.zh: 中宗不能窮也，詔琬與楚客、處訥約兄弟兩解之，故世謂帝為「和事天子」。

translations.literal: Zhongzong could not pursue the matter to the end; he ordered Wan, Chuke, and Chuna to pledge brotherhood and settle the dispute, wherefore the age called the emperor the "Peacemaking Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong would not press the case; he had Wan, Chuke, and Chuna swear brotherhood and make peace, and people nicknamed him the "Peacemaking Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書令。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 韋氏敗，與晉卿同誅。

translations.literal: When the Wei faction fell, he was executed together with Jinqing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei faction collapsed, he was executed along with Jinqing.

sentences.zh: 楚客性明達。

translations.literal: Chuke was by nature clear-sighted and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was by nature shrewd and far-seeing.

sentences.zh: 武後時，降突厥沓實力吐敦者，部落在平夏。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, the surrendered Turk Tashili Tutun—whose tribe was at Pingxia—
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, the surrendered Turk Tashili Tutun had his people at Pingxia.

sentences.zh: 會邊書至，言吐敦反，楚客為兵部員外郎，後召問方略，對曰：「吐敦者，臣昔與之言，其為人忠義和厚，且國家與有恩必不反。

translations.literal: When a border report arrived saying Tutun had rebelled, Chuke was a vice director in the Ministry of War; the empress later summoned him and asked his plan; he replied: "Tashili—I once spoke with him; as a man he is loyal, righteous, and generous, and the state has shown him kindness, so he will surely not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier dispatches reported that Tutun had risen in revolt, Chuke was a vice director in the ministry of war; the empress later asked his view, and he said, "Tashili I know from conversation: he is loyal, just, and steady, and the court has treated him well—he will not rebel.

sentences.zh: 其兄之子默子者，狡悍，與吐敦不和，今言叛，疑默子為之，然無能為。」

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Mozi is cunning and fierce and at odds with Tutun; the present report of rebellion, I suspect, is Mozi's doing, yet he is incapable of accomplishing anything."
translations.idiomatic: His brother's son Mozi is crafty and violent and hates Tutun; I suspect this report comes from Mozi, though he lacks the power to do much harm."

sentences.zh: 俄而夏州表默子劫部落北奔，為州兵及吐敦所擒。

translations.literal: Soon a report from Xiazhou stated that Mozi had seized the tribe and fled north, but was captured by the prefectural troops and Tutun.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiazhou reported that Mozi had seized the tribe and fled north, only to be taken by the prefectural force and Tutun.

sentences.zh: 後張仁亶請築三城，議者或不同，獨楚客言：「萬世利也。」

translations.literal: Later Zhang Renbian requested building three fortresses; some in the deliberations disagreed, but Chuke alone said: "It would benefit ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Renbian proposed building three frontier forts and some at court objected, Chuke alone said, "The gain would last ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 然冒於權利，嘗諷右補闕趙廷禧陳符命以媚帝，曰：「唐有天下，當百世繼周，陛下承母禪，周、唐一統，其符兆有八：天皇再以陛下為周王，是在唐興周，則天立陛下為皇太子，是在周興唐，一也；

translations.literal: Yet he was reckless in pursuit of profit and power; he once induced Right Remonstrance Councillor Zhao Yanxi to present portents to flatter the emperor, saying: "Tang holds the realm and should succeed Zhou for a hundred generations; Your Majesty received the abdication from your mother; Zhou and Tang are unified—the portents number eight: Heaven's Empress twice made Your Majesty King of Zhou—this was Tang raising Zhou; Empress Zetian installed Your Majesty as crown prince—this was Zhou raising Tang—the first;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy for power and gain; he once prompted right remonstrance councillor Zhao Yanxi to parade omens before the throne, saying, "Tang holds the realm and is destined to succeed Zhou for a hundred generations; Your Majesty received the throne from your mother, uniting Zhou and Tang—and the signs are eight: the Heavenly Empress twice made you King of Zhou, which was Tang raising Zhou; Empress Zetian then made you crown prince, which was Zhou raising Tang—the first;

sentences.zh: 天後立文王廟，二也；

translations.literal: The Empress Zetian established a temple to King Wen—the second;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian built a temple to King Wen—the second;

sentences.zh: 唐同泰《洛水圖》云：『永昌帝業』，三也；

translations.literal: Tang Tongtai's "Chart of the Luo River" says: "An empire of eternal prosperity"—the third;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Tongtai's Chart of the Luo River reads, "An empire of eternal prosperity"—the third;

sentences.zh: 讖曰：『百代不移宗』，四也；

translations.literal: A prophecy says: "The ancestral line will not shift for a hundred generations"—the fourth;
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy says, "The ancestral line will not shift for a hundred generations"—the fourth;

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『百世繼周』，五也；

translations.literal: Confucius said: "A hundred generations succeeding Zhou"—the fifth;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "A hundred generations succeeding Zhou"—the fifth;

sentences.zh: 《桑條韋歌》，應二聖在位九十八年，而子孫相承九十八世，六也；

translations.literal: The "Mulberry-branch Wei Song" corresponds to the two sages reigning ninety-eight years, and descendants succeeding for ninety-eight generations—the sixth;
translations.idiomatic: The Mulberry-branch Wei Song matches two sage rulers reigning ninety-eight years and ninety-eight generations of heirs—the sixth;

sentences.zh: 乃二月慶雲五色，天應以和，七也；

translations.literal: Then in the second month auspicious clouds of five colors appeared—heaven responded with harmony—the seventh;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month five-colored auspicious clouds appeared—heaven answering in harmony—the seventh;

sentences.zh: 去六月九日，內出瑞蒜，八也。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the sixth month last year, an auspicious garlic sprouted within the palace—the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the sixth month last year an auspicious garlic sprout appeared within the palace—the eighth.

sentences.zh: 起則天為一世，聖朝為二世，後子孫相承九十八，其數正滿百世，唐之歷乃三千余年。」

translations.literal: Counting Empress Zetian as one generation and the sacred dynasty as the second, with descendants succeeding for ninety-eight more, the number exactly fills a hundred generations—Tang's calendar will span more than three thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Take Empress Zetian as one age and the sacred reign as the second; add ninety-eight generations of heirs and the count reaches exactly one hundred—Tang's span will run three thousand years and more."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，擢延禧諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrance and Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and promoted Yanxi to remonstrance and counsel.

sentences.zh: 識者以楚客等欺神誣君，且有大咎。

translations.literal: Those who understood held that Chuke and his ilk were deceiving the spirits and hoodwinking the sovereign, and would meet great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment said Chuke and his sort were fooling heaven and deceiving the throne, and would bring down grave disaster.

sentences.zh: 又嘗密語其黨曰：「始，吾在卑位，尤愛宰相；

translations.literal: He also once said secretly to his faction: "At first, when I was in a low position, I especially coveted the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: He also confided once to his followers: "At first, in a humble post, I wanted nothing so much as the chancellorship;

sentences.zh: 及居之，又思天子，南面一日足矣。」

translations.literal: once I held it, I then thought of the Son of Heaven—facing south for a single day would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: once I had it, I began to think of the throne itself—even one day facing south would be enough."

sentences.zh: 雖外附韋氏，而內畜逆謀，故卒以敗。

translations.literal: Although outwardly he attached to the Wei faction, inwardly he harbored treasonous designs—therefore he ended in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he clung to the Wei faction, but inwardly he nursed rebellion, and so came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 晉卿髭貌雄偉，聲如鐘。

translations.literal: Jinqing had a mustache and appearance that were heroic and imposing; his voice was like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing bore a fierce mustache and a towering presence; his voice rang like a bell.

sentences.zh: 雖不學，然性倜儻。

translations.literal: Although unlettered, he was by nature free-spirited and bold.
translations.idiomatic: He had little learning, but his temperament was bold and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 垂拱後，武後任之，宮苑、閑廄、內外眾作無不總。

translations.literal: After the Chuigong era, Empress Wu employed him, and he had overall charge of palace gardens, idle stables, and all construction projects inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chuigong era, Empress Wu put him in charge of palace gardens, the imperial stables, and every building project within and beyond the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 開中嶽，造明堂，鑄九鼎，有力焉。

translations.literal: In opening Mount Song as the central peak, building the Bright Hall, and casting the Nine Cauldrons, he contributed significantly.
translations.idiomatic: He played a major part in elevating Mount Song as the central sacred peak, constructing the Bright Hall, and casting the Nine Cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 紀處訥者，秦州上邽人。

translations.literal: Ji Chune was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Chune came from Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為人魁岸，髭長數尺。

translations.literal: He was a man of towering build, with a beard several feet long.
translations.idiomatic: A man of imposing stature, he wore a beard several feet long.

sentences.zh: 其妻武三思婦之姊，縱使通三思，繇是款昵，進為太府卿。

translations.literal: His wife was the elder sister of Wu Sansi's wife. She encouraged him to cultivate ties with Sansi; through this intimate connection he was promoted to Grand Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the elder sister of Wu Sansi's wife. She urged him to cultivate Sansi, and through that close tie he rose to grand minister of the palace treasury.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年夏，大旱，谷價騰踴，中宗召問所以救人者。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Shenlong, a great drought caused grain prices to soar. Emperor Zhongzong summoned officials to ask what could be done to save the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Shenlong 1, severe drought sent grain prices soaring. Emperor Zhongzong summoned his ministers to ask how the people might be saved.

sentences.zh: 三思知之，陰諷太史迦葉誌忠奏「是夜攝提入太微，近帝坐，此天子與大臣接，有納忠之符」。

translations.literal: Sansin learned of this and secretly prompted the court astronomer Ye Zhizhong to memorialized: "That night Sheti entered the Taiwei constellation near the imperial seat—this signifies the Son of Heaven meeting with his ministers and is an omen of receiving loyal counsel."
translations.idiomatic: When Sansi learned of this, he secretly urged the court astronomer Ye Zhizhong to memorialized that "on that night Sheti entered Taiwei near the imperial seat—meaning the Son of Heaven is meeting his ministers, a sign that loyal counsel will be received."

sentences.zh: 帝信之，下詔褒美，賜處訥衣一副、彩六十段。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it, issued an edict praising him, and bestowed on Chune one set of garments and sixty bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him, issued an edict of praise, and granted Chune one set of robes and sixty bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 與楚客並同三品，進侍中。

translations.literal: He was made equal in rank to the Third Grade together with Chuke, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was ranked equal to the third grade together with Chuke and promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後伏誅。

translations.literal: Later he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later executed.

sentences.zh: 祝欽明字文思，京兆始平人。

translations.literal: Zhu Qinming, courtesy name Wensi, was a native of Shiping in the Jingzhao region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qinming, styled Wensi, was from Shiping in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父綝，字叔良，少通經，頗著書質諸家疑異；

translations.literal: His father Shen, courtesy name Shuliang, mastered the Classics in youth and wrote extensively to settle doubts and discrepancies among the various schools;
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen, styled Shuliang, mastered the classics in youth and wrote widely to resolve the doubts and discrepancies of the various schools;

sentences.zh: 門人張後胤既顯宦，薦於朝，詔對策高第，終無極尉。

translations.literal: When his disciple Zhang Houyin rose to high office, he recommended him to the court. An edict ordered him to answer policy questions and placed him at the top; he ended his career as magistrate of Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: When his disciple Zhang Houyin rose to high office, he recommended Shen to the court. An edict summoned him to answer policy questions; he placed at the top and ended as magistrate of Wuji.

sentences.zh: 欽明擢明經，為東臺典儀。

translations.literal: Qinming passed the Mingjing examination and became Director of Rites for the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming passed the mingjing examination and served as director of rites for the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 永淳、天授間，又中英才傑出、業奧《六經》等科，拜著作郎，為太子率更令。

translations.literal: Between the Yongchun and Tianshou eras he also passed the examinations for Outstanding Talent and for Mastery of the "Six Classics," was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library, and served as Director of Palace Works for the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yongchun and Tianshou he also passed the examinations for outstanding talent and for mastery of the "Six Classics," was appointed gentleman of the palace library, and served as the crown prince's director of palace works.

sentences.zh: 中宗在東宮，欽明兼侍讀，授太子經，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: While Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace, Qinming served concurrently as Lecturer to the Heir, teaching the Classics to the crown prince, and as a scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was crown prince, Qinming served concurrently as his lecturing attendant, teaching him the classics, and as a scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，擢國子祭酒、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong regained the throne, Qinming was promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and Vice Chairman of the Chancellery under the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored to the throne, Qinming was made chancellor of the directorate of education and vice chairman of the chancellery under the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 進禮部尚書，封魯國公，食實封戶三百。

translations.literal: He was further made Minister of Rites, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, with three hundred households for his substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to minister of rites, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, with three hundred households for his substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 桓彥範、崔玄暐、袁恕巳，敬暉等皆從受《周官》大義，朝廷尊之。

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan, Cui Xuanwei, Yuan Shuji, Jing Hui, and others all received instruction from him in the grand meaning of the "Rites of Zhou," and the court held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan, Cui Xuanwei, Yuan Shuji, Jing Hui, and others all studied under him the grand meaning of the "Rites of Zhou," and the court honored him.

sentences.zh: 以匿親忌日，為御史中丞蕭至忠所劾，貶申州刺史。

translations.literal: Because he concealed the anniversary of a parent's death, he was impeached by Imperial Censor-in-Chief Xiao Zhizhong and demoted to prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he concealed a parent's death anniversary, he was impeached by imperial censor-in-chief Xiao Zhizhong and demoted to prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve again as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve again as chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，天子將郊，欽明與國子司業郭山惲陰迎韋後意，謬立議曰：

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, when the Son of Heaven was about to perform the suburban sacrifice, Qinming and Vice Chancellor Guo Shanyun secretly catered to Empress Wei's wishes and put forward a twisted argument, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 3, as the emperor prepared for the suburban sacrifice, Qinming and vice chancellor Guo Shanyun secretly catered to Empress Wei and offered a perverse argument, saying:

sentences.zh: 《周官》天神曰祀，地祗曰祭，宗廟曰享。

translations.literal: In the "Rites of Zhou," heavenly spirits are called si, earthly spirits jiao, and ancestral temples xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" says that heavenly spirits are called si, earthly spirits jiao, and ancestral temples xiang.

sentences.zh: 《大宗伯》曰：「祀大神，祭大祗，享大鬼，王有故不預，則攝而薦。

translations.literal: The "Chief Minister of Rites" states: "In sacrificing to the great spirits, offering to the great earthly powers, and feasting the great ghosts—if the king has pressing affairs and cannot attend, then one acts in his stead and presents the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The "Chief Minister of Rites" says: "When sacrificing to the great spirits, offering to the great earthly powers, and feasting the great ghosts, if the king has pressing business and cannot attend, another acts in his stead and presents the offerings.

sentences.zh: 追師掌後首服，以待祭祀。

translations.literal: The Master of Robes for the Queen manages the queen's ceremonial headgear for use in sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The master of robes for the queen keeps the queen's ceremonial headgear ready for sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 內司服掌後六服，祭祀則供。

translations.literal: The Inner Director of Robes supervises the queen's six kinds of ritual garments and supplies them for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The inner director of robes supervises the queen's six ritual garments and provides them for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又九嬪，凡大祭祀，後裸獻則贊瑤爵。

translations.literal: Again, among the nine concubines—at all great sacrifices, when the queen performs the unclothed offering, she assists by presenting the jade cup.
translations.idiomatic: Among the nine concubines, at every great sacrifice when the queen performs the unclothed offering, she assists by presenting the jade cup.

sentences.zh: 然則後當助天子祀天神、祭地只。

translations.literal: Thus the queen ought to assist the Son of Heaven in sacrificing to the spirits of Heaven and offering to the spirits of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the queen should assist the Son of Heaven in sacrificing to the spirits of Heaven and offering to the spirits of Earth.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄稱：闕狄，後助王祭群小祀服。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: Qu Di is the robe by which the queen assists the king in sacrificing at all minor rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says that the Qu Di robe is what the queen wears when assisting the king at all minor sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 小祀尚助，況天地哉？

translations.literal: If she assists even at minor rites, how much more at rites to Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: If she assists at minor rites, how much more should she assist at rites to Heaven and Earth!

sentences.zh: 闕狄之上，祎、褕、狄，三服皆以助祭，知祎衣助大祀也。

translations.literal: Above Qu Di are the Yi, Yu, and Di robes—three garments all used to assist in sacrifice—showing that the Yi robe assists at great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Above the Qu Di are the Yi, Yu, and Di robes—three garments all used to assist in sacrifice—showing that the Yi robe assists at great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王之祭服二：曰先王兗冕，先公冕。

translations.literal: The king has two sacrificial robes: the Yan cap and robe for former kings, and the Gong cap and robe for former lords.
translations.idiomatic: The king has two sacrificial robes: the yan cap and robe for former kings, and the gong cap and robe for former lords.

sentences.zh: 故後助祭，亦以祎衣祭先王，褕狄祭先公。

translations.literal: Therefore, when the queen assists in sacrifice, she likewise uses the Yi robe in sacrificing to former kings and the Yu and Di robes in sacrificing to former lords.
translations.idiomatic: When the queen assists in sacrifice, she likewise uses the Yi robe for former kings and the Yu and Di robes for former lords.

sentences.zh: 不言助祭天地，舉此以明彼，反三隅也。
