translations.literal: Though the text does not explicitly mention assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, one cites this to illuminate that—the method of inferring the whole from one side.
translations.idiomatic: Though the text does not explicitly mention assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, one cites this to clarify that—the method of inferring the rest from one corner.

sentences.zh: 《春秋外傳》：禘郊，天子親射其牛，王後親春其粢。」

translations.literal: The "Outer Commentary on the Spring and Autumn" says: At the di and suburban rites, the Son of Heaven personally shoots the sacrificial ox, and the queen personally pounds the sacrificial grain."
translations.idiomatic: The "Outer Commentary on the Spring and Autumn" says that at the di and suburban rites, the Son of Heaven personally shoots the sacrificial ox and the queen personally pounds the sacrificial grain."

sentences.zh: 世婦詔後之禮事，不專主宗廟。

translations.literal: The Supervisor of Harem Women instructs the queen in ritual affairs and does not deal exclusively with the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor of harem women instructs the queen in ritual affairs and does not deal exclusively with the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 《祭統》曰：「祭也者，必夫婦親之，所以備內外之官。」

translations.literal: The "Record of Sacrificial Matters" states: "Sacrifice must be performed in person by husband and wife, so that both inner and outer offices are fully staffed."
translations.idiomatic: The "Record of Sacrificial Matters" says: "Sacrifice must be performed in person by husband and wife, so that both inner and outer offices are fully represented."

sentences.zh: 哀公問孔子曰：「冕而親迎，不已重乎？」

translations.literal: Duke Ai asked Confucius: "To wear the ceremonial cap and go in person to meet one's bride—is that not excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai asked Confucius: "To wear the ceremonial cap and go in person to meet one's bride—is that not going too far?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「合二姓之好，以繼先聖之後，以為天地宗廟社稷主，君何謂已重焉？」

translations.literal: He answered: "To unite two surnames in marriage, to continue the line of former sages, and to become master of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain—how can Your Lordship call that excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "To unite two surnames in marriage, to continue the line of former sages, and to become master of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain—how can you call that excessive?"

sentences.zh: 則知後宜助祭。

translations.literal: From this we know the queen ought to assist in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know the queen should assist in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 臣請因經誼，制儀典。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that, in accordance with the meaning of the classics, ritual regulations be established.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that ritual regulations be established in accordance with the meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不睿，猶疑之，召禮官質問。

translations.literal: Though the emperor lacked keen judgment, he still had doubts and summoned ritual officials to examine the question.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was not sharp-witted, he still had doubts and summoned ritual officials to examine the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒對：「欽明所引，皆宗廟禮，非祭天地者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu replied: "What Qinming cites is all ancestral-temple ritual, not rites for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon erudites of the court of imperial sacrifices Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu replied: "What Qinming cites is all ancestral-temple ritual, not rites for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 周、隋而上，無皇后助祭事。」

translations.literal: From Zhou down through Sui, there is no record of an empress assisting in sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou through Sui, there is no record of an empress assisting in sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 帝令宰相參訂，紹、欽緒又引博士彭景直共議曰：

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief ministers to adjudicate. Shao and Qinxu further cited Erudite Peng Jingzhi to join in deliberation and said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chief ministers to adjudicate. Shao and Qinxu further brought in erudite Peng Jingzhi to join the deliberation and said:

sentences.zh: 《周官》所雲祀、祭、享，皆互言。

translations.literal: In the "Rites of Zhou," where si, jiao, and xiang are spoken of, the terms are used interchangeably.
translations.idiomatic: In the "Rites of Zhou," where si, jiao, and xiang are mentioned, the terms are used interchangeably.

sentences.zh: 《典瑞》：「兩圭以祀地。」

translations.literal: The "Regulations on Jade Insignia" states: "Two gui tablets are used in sacrificing to Earth."
translations.idiomatic: The "Regulations on Jade Insignia" says: "Two gui tablets are used in sacrificing to Earth."

sentences.zh: 《司几筵》：「設祀先王昨席。」

translations.literal: The "Director of Ritual Mats" states: "Set out the mat for sacrificing to former kings."
translations.idiomatic: The "Director of Ritual Mats" says: "Set out the mat for sacrificing to former kings."

sentences.zh: 《內宗》：「掌宗廟祭祀。」

translations.literal: The "Inner Superintendent" states: "Has charge of ancestral-temple sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: The "Inner Superintendent" says: "Has charge of ancestral-temple sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「聖人為能饗帝。」

translations.literal: The transmitted text says: "The sage is able to feast the Lord on High."
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text says: "The sage is able to feast the Lord on High."

sentences.zh: 「春秋祭祀，以時思之。」

translations.literal: "The sacrifices of spring and autumn are performed in season as tokens of remembrance."
translations.idiomatic: "The sacrifices of spring and autumn are performed in season as tokens of remembrance."

sentences.zh: 此祀天稱享，享廟稱祭也。

translations.literal: Here sacrificing to Heaven is called xiang, and feasting the temple is called jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Here sacrificing to Heaven is called xiang, and feasting the temple is called jiao.

sentences.zh: 禮家凡稱大祭祀，不獨主天。

translations.literal: When ritualists speak of "great sacrifice" in general, it does not refer to Heaven alone.
translations.idiomatic: When ritualists speak of a great sacrifice in general, it does not refer to Heaven alone.

sentences.zh: 《爵人》：「大祭祀，與量人受舉斝之卒爵。」

translations.literal: The "Cupbearer" states: "At the great sacrifice, together with the Metrologist he receives the final libation cup."
translations.idiomatic: The "Cupbearer" says: "At the great sacrifice, together with the metrologist he receives the final libation cup."

sentences.zh: 祭天不祼，則九嬪贊瑤爵，容廟稱大祭祀也。

translations.literal: Since sacrifice to Heaven does not involve the unclothed offering, yet the nine concubines assist with the jade cup, this shows that "great sacrifice" can refer to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Since sacrifice to Heaven does not involve the unclothed offering, yet the nine concubines assist with the jade cup, this shows that "great sacrifice" can refer to the temple.

sentences.zh: 欽明據《大宗伯》之職，以謂後有祭天地之禮。

translations.literal: Qinming, relying on the duties of the "Chief Minister of Rites," concluded that the queen had rites for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming, relying on the duties of the "Chief Minister of Rites," argued that the queen had rites for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 按經：「凡祀大神、祭大祗、享大鬼，帥執事而卜宿，視滌濯，涖玉鬯，省牲鑊，奉玉盥，制大號。

translations.literal: Examining the classic: "For all sacrifices to great spirits, offerings to great earthly powers, and feasts for great ghosts—leading the officiants to divination for the day, inspecting cleansing, overseeing the libation jade, reviewing the sacrificial cauldrons, presenting the jade and wash, and issuing the great proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the classic: "For all sacrifices to great spirits, offerings to great earthly powers, and feasts for great ghosts—leading the officiants to divination for the day, inspecting cleansing, overseeing the libation jade, reviewing the sacrificial cauldrons, presenting the jade and wash, and issuing the great proclamation.

sentences.zh: 若王不與祭祀，則攝位。」

translations.literal: If the king does not join the sacrifice, then one assumes his position."
translations.idiomatic: If the king does not join the sacrifice, then one assumes his position."

sentences.zh: 自凡而推，兼言王祭天地宗廟也。

translations.literal: Starting from this general statement and extending it, the text speaks comprehensively of the king sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Starting from this general statement and extending it, the text speaks comprehensively of the king sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 下言：「凡大祭祀，王後不與，則攝而薦。」

translations.literal: Below it states: "For all great sacrifices, if the queen does not attend, then one acts in her stead and presents the offerings."
translations.idiomatic: Below it states: "For all great sacrifices, if the queen does not attend, then one acts in her stead and presents the offerings."

sentences.zh: 直王後祭廟一凡耳。

translations.literal: This refers only to one general rule concerning the queen's sacrifices at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: This refers only to one general rule concerning the queen's sacrifices at the temple.

sentences.zh: 若當助祭天地，應不列重凡。

translations.literal: If she were to assist at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, there ought not to be a repeated general statement.
translations.idiomatic: If she were to assist at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, there ought not to be a repeated general statement.

sentences.zh: 且內宗、外宗所掌，皆佐王後廟薦，無佐祭天地語。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the Inner and Outer Superintendents supervise is all assisting the queen at temple offerings; there is no language about assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what the inner and outer superintendents supervise is all assisting the queen at temple offerings; there is no language about assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 有如助祭天地，誰當贊佐者？

translations.literal: If she were to assist at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, who would assist her?
translations.idiomatic: If she were to assist at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, who would assist her?

sentences.zh: 是則攝薦為宗廟明甚。

translations.literal: Thus it is perfectly clear that acting in stead and presenting offerings refers to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is perfectly clear that acting in stead and presenting offerings refers to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 內司服掌後祭服，無祭天服。

translations.literal: The Inner Director of Robes manages the queen's sacrificial garments; there is no garment for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The inner director of robes manages the queen's sacrificial garments; there is no garment for sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禮家說曰：「後不助祭天地五嶽，故無具服。」

translations.literal: Ritualists explain: "The queen does not assist in sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and the Five Sacred Peaks, and therefore has no complete ritual garb for those rites."
translations.idiomatic: Ritualists explain: "The queen does not assist in sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and the Five Sacred Peaks, and therefore has no complete ritual garb for those rites."

sentences.zh: 又言：「後有五輅，以重翟從祭先王先公，以厭翟從饗諸侯，以安車朝夕見王，以翟車采桑，以輦車遊宴。」

translations.literal: It also states: "The queen has five carriages—using the Chongdi carriage to follow in sacrificing to former kings and lords, the Yandi carriage to follow in feasting the feudal lords, the Anche for morning and evening audiences with the king, the Diche for gathering mulberry leaves, and the Nian carriage for leisurely excursions."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "The queen has five carriages—using the chongdi carriage to follow in sacrificing to former kings and lords, the yandi carriage to follow in feasting the feudal lords, the anche for morning and evening audiences with the king, the diche for gathering mulberry leaves, and the nian carriage for leisurely excursions."

sentences.zh: 按此，後無祭天車明甚。

translations.literal: From this it is perfectly clear that the queen has no carriage for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is perfectly clear that the queen has no carriage for sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 然後助王祭天地，古無聞焉。

translations.literal: Yet that the queen should assist the king in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth—never has this been heard of in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that the queen should assist the king in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth—never has this been heard of in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射韋巨源助後掎掣帝，奪政事，即傳欽明議，帝果用其言，以皇后為亞獻。

translations.literal: At that time Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan, aiding the empress in restraining the emperor and seizing governmental affairs, immediately circulated Qinming's proposal; the emperor indeed adopted it and made the empress secondary offerer.
translations.idiomatic: At that time left vice director Wei Juyuan, aiding the empress in restraining the emperor and seizing governmental affairs, immediately circulated Qinming's proposal; the emperor adopted it and made the empress secondary offerer.

sentences.zh: 取大臣李嶠等女為齋娘，奉豆籩。

translations.literal: Daughters of chief ministers such as Li Jiao were selected as purification maidens to present the dou and bian vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters of chief ministers such as Li Jiao were chosen as purification maidens to present the dou and bian vessels.

sentences.zh: 禮成，詔齋娘有夫者悉進官。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, an edict ordered that all purification maidens who had husbands were promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, an edict ordered that all purification maidens who had husbands be promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 初，後屬婚，上食禁中，帝與群臣宴，欽明自言能《八風舞》，帝許之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the empress's clan was arranging a marriage, a feast was held within the palace; the emperor banqueted with his ministers. Qinming declared that he could perform the "Dance of the Eight Winds," and the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the empress's clan was arranging a marriage, a feast was held within the palace. The emperor banqueted with his ministers, and Qinming declared that he could perform the "Dance of the Eight Winds"; the emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 欽明體肥醜，據地搖頭睆目，左右顧眄，帝大笑。

translations.literal: Qinming was fat and ugly; crouching on the ground he wagged his head, rolled his eyes, and looked about left and right. The emperor roared with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming was fat and ugly. Crouching on the ground he wagged his head, rolled his eyes, and glanced left and right, and the emperor roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎盧藏用嘆曰：「是舉《五經》掃地矣！」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Zangyong sighed and said: "With this act the Five Classics have been swept onto the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: Vice minister of personnel Lu Zangyong sighed and said: "With this act the Five Classics have been swept onto the ground!"

sentences.zh: 景雲初，侍御史倪若水劾奏：「欽明、山惲等腐儒無行，以諂佞亂常改作，百王所傳，一朝惰放。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun, Remonstrating Censor Ni Ruoshui impeached them, saying: "Qinming, Shanyun, and others are corrupt Ruists without character who, through flattery and sycophancy, overturned established practice in a single morning, casting aside what a hundred kings transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingyun, remonstrating censor Ni Ruoshui impeached them, saying: "Qinming, Shanyun, and others are corrupt Ruists without character who, through flattery and sycophancy, overturned established practice in a single morning, casting aside what a hundred kings transmitted.

sentences.zh: 今聖德中興，不宜使小人在朝，請斥遠之，以肅具臣。」

translations.literal: Now that sagely virtue is restored, it is unfitting to keep petty men at court. We request that they be dismissed and sent far away, so that upright ministers may be kept in proper order."
translations.idiomatic: Now that sagely virtue is restored, it is unfitting to keep petty men at court. We request that they be dismissed and sent far away, so that upright ministers may be kept in proper order."

sentences.zh: 乃貶欽明饒州刺史，山惲括州刺史。

translations.literal: Qinming was demoted to prefect of Raozhou and Shanyun to prefect of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming was demoted to prefect of Raozhou and Shanyun to prefect of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 欽明於《五經》為該淹，自見坐不孝免，無以澡祓，乃阿附韋氏，圖再用，又坐是見逐，諸儒共羞之。

translations.literal: Qinming was thoroughly versed in the "Five Classics." After he was dismissed for the offense of filial impiety, finding no means of purification, he attached himself to the Wei clan in hope of reinstatement; again for this he was driven out, and all the Confucians shared in the shame.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming was thoroughly versed in the "Five Classics." After he was dismissed for filial impiety, finding no means of purification, he attached himself to the Wei clan in hope of reinstatement; again for this he was driven out, and all the Confucians shared in the shame.

sentences.zh: 後徙洪州都督，入為崇文館學士，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to serve as Protector-General of Hongzhou, was recalled as a scholar of the Chongwen Institute, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to protector-general of Hongzhou, recalled as a scholar of the Chongwen Institute, and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：欽明以經授中宗，為朝大儒，乃詭聖僻說，引艷妻郊見上帝，腥德播聞，享胙不終。

translations.literal: The eulogy states: Qinming taught the classics to Zhongzong and was the court's great Confucian—yet he twisted the sages with perverse doctrines, leading a splendid consort to meet the Lord on High at the suburban rite. His tainted virtue became notorious, and he did not live out his full share of sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy states: Qinming taught the classics to Zhongzong and was the court's great Confucian—yet he twisted the sages with perverse doctrines, leading a splendid consort to meet the Lord on High at the suburban rite. His tainted virtue became notorious, and he did not live out his full share of sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 蓋與少正卯順非而澤，莊周以詩書破冢者同科。

translations.literal: He belongs in the same category as Shaozheng Mao, who affirmed what was wrong and spread it with gloss, and Zhuang Zhou, who used the "Odes" and "Documents" to break open tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He belongs in the same category as Shaozheng Mao, who affirmed what was wrong and spread it with gloss, and Zhuang Zhou, who used the "Odes" and "Documents" to break open tombs.

sentences.zh: 獨保腰領死家簀，寧不幸邪！

translations.literal: Yet he alone preserved neck and waist and died in his own bed—is that not good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he alone preserved neck and waist and died in his own bed—is that not good fortune!

sentences.zh: 後之托儒為奸者，可少戒云。

translations.literal: Let later men who would use Confucianism as a cloak for wickedness take some warning from this.
translations.idiomatic: Let later men who would use Confucianism as a cloak for wickedness take some warning from this.

sentences.zh: 山惲者，河東人。

translations.literal: Shanyun was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyun was a man of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 善治《禮》。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the study of the "Rites."
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in the study of the "Rites."

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷國子司業。

translations.literal: During Jinglong he was promoted step by step to Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong he rose step by step to vice chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 帝昵宴近臣及修文學士，詔遍為伎。

translations.literal: The emperor, fond of banqueting with close ministers and Cultivated Talent scholars, ordered all present to perform an art.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, fond of banqueting with close ministers and cultivated-talent scholars, ordered everyone present to perform an art.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書張錫為《談容娘舞》，將作大匠宗晉卿為《渾脫舞》，左衛將軍張洽為《黃麞舞》，給事中李行言歌《賀車西河曲》，余臣各有所陳，皆鄙黷；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Xi performed the "Dance of Lady Tanrong"; Chief Architect Zong Jinqing the "Huntuo Dance"; General of the Left Guard Zhang Qia the "Dance of the Yellow Deer"; Supervising Censor Li Xingyan sang "The Ballad of Heche and Xihe"; the remaining ministers each presented something—all were vulgar and improper;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of works Zhang Xi performed the "Dance of Lady Tanrong"; chief architect Zong Jinqing the "Huntuo Dance"; general of the left guard Zhang Qia the "Dance of the Yellow Deer"; supervising censor Li Xingyan sang "The Ballad of Heche and Xihe"; the remaining ministers each presented something—all vulgar and improper;

sentences.zh: 而出惲奏：「我所習，惟知誦詩。」

translations.literal: but when Shanyun's turn came he said: "What I practice is only reciting poetry."
translations.idiomatic: But when Shanyun's turn came he said: "What I practice is only reciting poetry."

sentences.zh: 乃誦《鹿鳴》、《蟋蟀》二篇，未畢，中書令李嶠以其近規諷，止之。

translations.literal: He then recited the two pieces "Deer Call" and "Cricket," but before he finished, Director of the Chancellery Li Jiao, because they came close to remonstrance and satire, stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited the two pieces "Deer Call" and "Cricket," but before he finished, director of the chancellery Li Jiao, because they came close to remonstrance and satire, stopped him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其直，下詔褒咨，賜服一稱。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his forthrightness, issued an edict commending him, and bestowed one set of garments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his forthrightness, issued an edict commending him, and bestowed one set of garments.

sentences.zh: 其後與欽明僻論阿世，不能終其守。

translations.literal: Later he joined Qinming in perverse arguments to flatter the times and could not hold to his integrity to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Qinming in perverse arguments to flatter the times and could not hold to his integrity to the end.

sentences.zh: 久之，復拜國子司業。

translations.literal: After some time he was again appointed Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was again appointed vice chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 王璵者，方慶六世孫，少為禮家學。

translations.literal: Wang Yu was a sixth-generation descendant of Fangqing and from youth studied the school of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was a sixth-generation descendant of Fangqing and from youth studied the school of rites.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在位久，推崇老子道，好神仙事，廣修祠祭，靡神不祈。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had been on the throne a long time. He exalted the Way of Laozi, loved affairs of immortals, expanded temples and sacrifices widely, and prayed to every spirit without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had reigned a long time. He exalted the Way of Laozi, loved affairs of immortals, expanded temples and sacrifices widely, and prayed to every spirit without exception.

sentences.zh: 璵上言，請築壇東郊祀青帝，天子入其言，擢太常博士、侍御史，為祠祭使。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized the throne, requesting that an altar be built in the eastern suburbs to sacrifice to the Green Lord; the Son of Heaven accepted his advice, promoted him to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Remonstrating Censor, and made him Commissioner of Temple Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized the throne, requesting that an altar be built in the eastern suburbs to sacrifice to the Green Lord. The emperor accepted his advice, promoted him to erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices and remonstrating censor, and made him commissioner of temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 璵專以祠解中帝意，有所禳祓，大抵類巫覡。

translations.literal: Yu specialized in interpreting sacrifices to hit the emperor's wishes; whatever exorcisms or purifications he undertook were for the most part like those of shamans.
translations.idiomatic: Yu specialized in interpreting sacrifices to suit the emperor's wishes; whatever exorcisms or purifications he undertook were for the most part like those of shamans.

sentences.zh: 漢以來葬喪皆有瘞錢，後世裏俗稍以紙寓錢為鬼事，至是璵乃用之。

translations.literal: Since Han times burials had included buried cash; later folk custom gradually used paper in place of money for ghostly affairs—and now Yu adopted the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times burials had included buried cash; later folk custom gradually used paper in place of money for ghostly affairs—and now Yu adopted the practice.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，累遷太常卿，又以祠禱見寵。

translations.literal: When Suzong was enthroned, [Yu] was repeatedly promoted until he became Minister of Rites, and again won favor through prayer offerings at shrines.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong took the throne, Yu rose to minister of rites and won favor again through shrine prayers.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年，拜蒲同絳等州節度使，俄以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyuan he was appointed Military Commissioner of Pu, Tong, Jiang, and other prefectures; soon after made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery and Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 3 he was made military commissioner over Pu, Tong, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures, and soon after vice director of the secretariat and associate chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時大兵後，天下願治，璵望輕，無它才，不為士議諧可，既驟得政，中外悵駭。

translations.literal: At the time, after great warfare, the realm longed for order; Yu's reputation was slight and he had no other talent; scholar-official opinion did not approve; once he suddenly gained power, court and countryside alike were dismayed and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The empire, exhausted by war, yearned for good government; Yu was lightly regarded and without other ability, and the literati did not trust him. When he suddenly entered government, court and country alike were appalled.

sentences.zh: 乃奏置太一壇，勸帝身見九宮祠。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to establish an altar to the Great Unity and urged the emperor to attend in person the shrine of the Nine Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for an altar to the Great Unity and urged the emperor to worship in person at the Nine Palaces shrine.

sentences.zh: 帝由是專意，它議不能奪。

translations.literal: The emperor from this devoted his mind to it, and other opinions could not sway him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fixed his heart on this, and no other counsel could move him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗不豫，太卜建言祟在山川。

translations.literal: The emperor once fell ill; the Grand Diviner proposed that the affliction lay in the mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, the grand diviner said the trouble came from the mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 璵遣女巫乘傳分禱天下名山大川，巫皆盛服，中人護領，所至幹托州縣，賂遺狼藉。

translations.literal: Yu sent shamans by relay post to pray separately at famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm; the shamans all wore splendid dress, eunuchs escorted them, and wherever they went they importuned the prefectures and counties, leaving bribes strewn about.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent witches by courier to pray at every famous peak and river. They traveled in rich robes under eunuch escort, and everywhere they went they shook down the local officials and left a trail of bribes.

sentences.zh: 時有一巫美而蠱，以惡少年數十自隨，尤憸狡不法。

translations.literal: At the time one shaman was beautiful and bewitching, followed by several dozen vicious youths, and was especially cunning, fierce, and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: One witch was beautiful and seductive, attended by dozens of rowdy youths, and was the most brazen and lawless of them all.

sentences.zh: 馳入黃州，刺史左震晨至館請事，門鐍不啟。

translations.literal: She galloped into Huangzhou; Prefect Zuo Zhen came early to the lodge to request an audience, but the door was bolted and would not open.
translations.idiomatic: She rode hard into Huangzhou. Prefect Zuo Zhen came at dawn to the inn to wait on her, but the door stayed bolted.

sentences.zh: 震怒，破鐍入，取巫斬廷下，悉誅所從少年，籍其贓得十余萬，因遣還中人。

translations.literal: Zhen was enraged; he broke the bolt and entered, seized the shaman and beheaded her in the courtyard, executed all the youths who followed her, registered their illicit gains at more than a hundred thousand, and sent the eunuch back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen in a fury broke the lock, dragged the witch out, and beheaded her in the courtyard; he killed every one of her followers, seized more than a hundred thousand in loot, and sent the eunuch escort home.

sentences.zh: 既以聞，璵不能詰，帝亦不加罪。

translations.literal: After this was reported, Yu could not pursue the matter, and the emperor also imposed no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Yu could not press the case, and the emperor imposed no penalty.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷璵為刑部尚書，又出為淮南節度使，猶兼祠祭使，徙浙東。

translations.literal: The next year Yu was removed to be Minister of Punishments, then sent out as Military Commissioner of Huainan, still concurrently Commissioner of Shrine Sacrifice, and later transferred to Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yu was shifted to minister of punishments, then posted as military commissioner of Huainan while still commissioner of shrine sacrifice, and later moved to Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 召入，再遷太子少師。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was again promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈開府儀同三司，謚曰簡懷。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given the rank of Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purse of the First Class; posthumous name Jianhuai.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored with the highest ceremonial rank and given the posthumous name Jianhuai, "Simple and Cherished."

sentences.zh: 始，璵托鬼神致位將相，當時以左道進者紛紛出焉。

translations.literal: At first Yu had relied on spirits and gods to reach the rank of minister and general; at the time those who advanced by heterodox ways came forth one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had first risen to minister and general through spirits and omens, and in his day many who advanced by unorthodox means followed the same path.

sentences.zh: 李國禎者，以術士顯，廣德初，建言「唐家仙系，宜崇表福區，招致神靈，請度昭應南山作天華上宮、露臺、大地婆父祠，並三皇、道君、太古天皇、中古伏羲、女媧等各為堂皇，給百戶掃除」。

translations.literal: Li Guozhen was a man who gained fame as a technician; at the beginning of Guangde he proposed: "The Tang imperial line of immortals should have its blessed domain exalted to summon spirits and gods; I request allotting Zhaoying's southern mountain to build the Upper Palace of Heavenly Splendor, the Terrace of Dew, and a shrine to the Great Earth Father-in-Law, and likewise separate halls for the Three August Ones, the Daoist Lords, the Primordial Heavenly Emperor, the Middle-Ancient Fuxi, Nüwa, and the rest, each with a hundred households assigned for sweeping and maintenance."
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen, a famous occultist, proposed early in the Guangde era that the Tang "immortal line" should mark out a sacred domain to draw down spirits: allot Mount Nan of Zhaoying for the Upper Palace of Heavenly Splendor, the Terrace of Dew, and a shrine to the Great Earth Father-in-Law, with separate halls for the Three Sovereigns, the Daoist lords, the primordial heavenly emperor, Fuxi, Nüwa, and the rest, each tended by a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又即義扶谷故湫祠龍，置房宇。

translations.literal: He also proposed at Yifugu's old dragon shrine at the sacred pool to erect buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He also wanted buildings raised at the old dragon pool shrine in Yifugu.

sentences.zh: 有詔從之，乃除地課工，方歲饑，人不堪命。

translations.literal: An edict approved this; land was levied and labor conscripted, but famine was then upon the year and the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented, levied land, and drafted labor just as famine gripped the land, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 昭應令梁鎮上疏切諫，以為有七不可：「天地之神，推之尊極者，掃地可祭，精意可享。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Zhaoying, Liang Zhen, submitted a sharp memorial of remonstrance, holding that there were seven points on which it could not be done: "The spirits of Heaven and Earth, when one pushes to the utmost of reverence, may be worshiped by sweeping the ground and received by sincere intent.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen, magistrate of Zhaoying, memorialized forcefully that the plan had seven fatal flaws: "The highest spirits of heaven and earth may be honored with a swept floor and a sincere heart.

sentences.zh: 今廢先王之典，為人祈福，福未至而人已困。

translations.literal: Now you abandon the institutions of the former kings to seek blessings for men—before blessings arrive the people are already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the rites of the former kings and pray for private blessing is to exhaust the people before any blessing arrives.

sentences.zh: 又違神虐人，何從而致福邪？

translations.literal: Moreover you violate the spirits and maltreat the people—how can blessings be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: To wrong the spirits and harm the people—how can that bring blessing?

sentences.zh: 宗廟月無三祭，此不宜然。

translations.literal: In the ancestral temple there are not three sacrifices in a month—this should not be so.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple does not hold three sacrifices in a month, and this should not be done.

sentences.zh: 婆父之鄙語，不經見，若為地建祖廟，上天必貽向背之責。

translations.literal: The vulgar term 'Father-in-Law of the Earth' is not found in the classics; if you build an ancestral temple for the earth, Heaven will surely send reproof of opposition.
translations.idiomatic: The vulgar title 'Earth Father-in-Law' appears in no classic; to build an earth temple is to invite heaven's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 夫湫者，龍所托耳，今湫竭已久，龍安所存？

translations.literal: A sacred pool is merely where a dragon lodges; now the pool has long been dry—where does the dragon dwell?
translations.idiomatic: A pool is only where a dragon rests, and this pool has been dry for ages—where is the dragon now?

sentences.zh: 不宜崇去龍之穴，破生人之產。

translations.literal: It is not fitting to exalt and abandon the dragon's lair while destroying the livelihood of the living.
translations.idiomatic: It is wrong to abandon the dragon's home and ruin the living people's means.

sentences.zh: 若三皇、五帝、道君等，兩京及所都各有宮廟，春秋彜饗，此復營造，是謂瀆神。

translations.literal: As for the Three August Ones, Five Emperors, Daoist Lords, and the like, the two capitals and each imperial residence already have palaces and temples with spring and autumn offerings—to build these again is to call it profaning the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sovereigns, Five Emperors, and Daoist lords already have temples in both capitals and every seat of rule, with spring and autumn sacrifices—to build more is to profane the gods.

sentences.zh: 夫休咎豐兇本於五事，不在山川百神明矣。」

translations.literal: Fortune and calamity, abundance and dearth, root in the Five Affairs and do not lie in the mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits and gods."
translations.idiomatic: Weal and woe, plenty and famine, depend on the Five Affairs, not on mountains, rivers, or a host of minor spirits."

sentences.zh: 即劾國禎等「動眾則得人，興工則獲利，祭祀則受胙，主執則市權，營罔天聽，負抱粢糈，道路相望，無時而息，人神胥怨，災孽並至。

translations.literal: He then impeached Guozhen and others: "When they move the masses they gain followers; when they raise works they reap profit; when they sacrifice they receive sacrificial flesh; when they preside they trade in power; they scheme to deceive Heaven's hearing; they bear offerings of grain on their backs; on the roads they press one upon another without cease; men and spirits alike resent them; disasters arrive together.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Guozhen and his party: "They gather crowds to win followers, launch projects for profit, take sacrificial meat from rites, sell influence as commissioners, deceive the throne, and march offerings along every road without rest until men and gods alike curse them and disasters multiply.

sentences.zh: 臣昨受命，有所安輯，陛下許以權宜，今所興造臣謹以便宜悉停」。

translations.literal: Your servant yesterday received a commission to bring calm, and Your Majesty granted discretionary authority; the constructions now begun your servant respectfully halts entirely as expedient."
translations.idiomatic: I was charged yesterday to restore order, and Your Majesty allowed me discretion; I now halt every project under way as an emergency measure."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 鎮忼慨有名士也，仕至司門郎中。

translations.literal: Zhen was indignant and high-minded, a man of reputation among scholars, and in office rose to Director of the Gate of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was a principled man of note among the literati and rose to director of the gate office in the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 璵曾孫摶，別傳。

translations.literal: Yu's great-grandson Tuan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's great-grandson Tuan is treated in a separate biography.
